messages.content:
Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Write the commitment surface in ordinary free prose, using whatever arrangement suits the content. You may distinguish a claim from a proposed application, scope, action or consequence; mention from dependence; a criticism and its grounds from a later use or revision; and an unresolved problem. None of these is required to exist. A proposed test, its relevance and the commitment itself can be criticized. State what you currently propose to take up without treating that as a truth certificate. Reference exposed material in prose where useful.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# commitment_return

Continue this account in light of the cross-examination. Decide which part of it bears on your account and what follows from that use.

## Original problem (task)
[5e2851f2d1f5e1aa] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input commitment_route (p.commitment_return.0)
[85708efd832d79ad] (h005.weave7.p.commitment_return.0)
Source commitment_route: daily/mini_prose/cycle-2/commitment_route; selected view: both
Artifact: 7df6d4bf71c6382c69c00188ef1d2d5570263592b92bb5e287dd0b322b2d8175
Original body SHA256: 43e0c6aab9f8f122dd5e6912d5906b83e0a2fa646a5c0ec36031993d667b7a92
Original commitments SHA256: 832f21ea774e672c1253b5b93b4dd87e9c5705d0f9e05d4454aa02c437b91861
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
I don't have the earlier body in front of me, only the commitments field of a prior contribution (p.commitment_route.0, artifact e3603e5417c60515505c7231dd23330d42e19c97190ac25360fd80708bfd5e6b). That view is enough to know what someone proposed to take up, but not enough to reproduce the argument that made the proposal seem worth taking up. I'll work from what the commitments disclose and flag where the missing body leaves me guessing.

What the commitments disclose is a package: a distinction between two questions — why later disagreements arise about the same words (with memory-gap and scope-ambiguity as compatible answers) and what the chores are expressing (with unequal baseline load as a third, different-kind answer); a per-person probe to be scored against pre-fixed clusters around scope, recurrence, or timing; and a move toward the avoidant flatmate that asks for their view of the group conversations rather than why they avoid them. The stated test: cluster -> proceed to a written local record; no cluster -> report no finding and specifically refuse to read non-clustering as support for an avoidance-as-central reading. The stated hedge: the account is a reading of material, not a diagnosis of people, and the hedge does not extend to the ordering of remedies, which the author declines to take up.

The gaps I can see from here, without the body, are the ones the commitments themselves flag. First, the memory-gap/scope-ambiguity separation is defended conceptually rather than by a case where the separation fails; I can't tell from the commitments alone whether that defense is an argument I'd accept or a stipulation, and no case is offered. Second, the probe's scoring rule is said to be fixed before the probe, but nothing in the commitments states the rule; I have the direction (clusters around scope, recurrence, timing) and the verdict categories (cluster / no cluster) but not the threshold or the coding scheme. Third, the non-clustering rule is explicitly conceded to be contestable, and I can't tell whether the concession is a genuine open point or a hedge the author already believes can be answered. Fourth, the move toward the avoidant flatmate is flagged as the most contestable part, and the facts it depends on — recency or chronicity of avoidance, whether the initiator is the avoided person, whether unequal load rather than memory gap is the friction — are not supplied by the commitments, and I have no view from here about whether they're available to the requester.

Given that, the honest claim I can make about the problem is structural rather than diagnostic. The dispute the requester describes has at least two separable loci: what was agreed (an event-and-record question) and what the agreement was for (a load-and-entitlement question). Agreements about chores are unusually vulnerable to the first kind of slippage because they're usually made verbally, restated in paraphrase, and indexed to schedules that change — flat 01274f41553299e7 says exactly that. The second kind of slippage is often invisible until someone starts avoiding, because avoidance protects the avoider from having to name a load complaint they may not have formulated. These two are not rivals. That much I'd take from the prior commitments without needing the body, because the commitments state it directly.

What I won't take from the commitments is the ordering of remedies, and the author of the prior commitment already declined that. I have no basis from here to say the probe should come before or after a conversation with the avoidant friend, or that a record is better than a reassignment. The prior commitment orders probe first and record as conditional, but names no criterion for why probe precedes talk. If I had to act, I would look at one thing the commitments don't mention: whether the avoidant flatmate's avoidance is recent. Recent avoidance after a specific exchange is a different phenomenon from long-standing avoidance after accumulated ones, and the commitments treat the avoidance as a single object. That's my addition, and it's a proposal, not a claim the prior commitments support.

What I'd actually put on the table now, as something to take up rather than something settled: write down, for each chore that's been argued about, (a) the last time it was agreed in words, who said what, and (b) the last time it was done and by whom. Do this privately, before any group conversation. If the (a) entries are thin or contradictory while the (b) entries are uneven across the three flatmates, that points toward the load question; if the (a) entries are specific but the (b) entries are roughly even, that points toward the meaning question. This is a reading aid, not a test with a threshold, and I don't know whether it would survive contact with the flatmates. It is also possible that writing anything down is itself a move in the argument, which the prior commitment's record-trial proposal already anticipated by calling it a 'local trial.'
COMMITMENTS
Taking this up means holding one claim that I think the prior commitments support, one proposal that they do not, and one gap I'm naming rather than filling.

The claim: the memory-gap reading and the scope-ambiguity reading are answers to 'why does the same wording get read differently later,' and the unequal-baseline-load reading is an answer to 'what is the chore disagreement doing in this flat.' These are not competitors. I am restating what p.commitment_route.0 already asserted, so this is not a new claim from me; it is a claim I'm willing to carry forward, and I'd be held to it if someone shows the two questions cannot be separated in a case like this one. The prior commitment already flags that vulnerability and reports no case where the separation fails. I have no case either.

The proposal (not a claim, and not derived from the prior commitments): write down the two-column record I sketched, privately and before any group conversation, and treat thin-and-contradictory memory entries alongside uneven load entries as pointing toward the load question, and specific memory entries alongside roughly even load entries as pointing toward the meaning question. I don't know if the requester can do this without it becoming public, and I don't know whether 'roughly even' can be judged by the requester without bias. Those are grounds on which the proposal could be criticized even before it is tried, and I'd want them stated now rather than after.

The gap I'm naming and not filling: I do not have the original body from p.commitment_route.0, so I cannot tell whether the conceptual argument for keeping the two questions separate was an argument or a stipulation, nor what the probe's pre-fixed scoring rule actually was. Anyone taking up this contribution should treat the probe description as incomplete here, not as a rule they can run. Non-clustering should not, under any reading, be treated as evidence for the avoidance-as-central reading; the prior commitment says this and I agree, but I'd add that non-clustering also should not be treated as evidence against it, only as evidence against the task-feature prediction.

What I am not committing to: that the probe should precede talking with the avoidant flatmate; that the requester is not themselves the avoided person; that the flat can talk without a mediator; that a reassignment, a mediator, or naming the avoidance as the problem would be worse than a record; that the prior commitment's order of remedies is wrong (I have no basis to say either way); or that recent avoidance differs in kind from long-standing avoidance in a way that should change what the requester does. The recency point is my addition and it is a proposal about what to look at, not a claim about what is true. A quiet week remains uninformative, and so does a week in which the record is written but not discussed.

## Selected input cross (p.commitment_return.1)
[56547505487057b2] (h005.weave7.p.commitment_return.1)
Source cross: daily/mini_prose/cycle-2/cross; selected view: both
Artifact: 88c4fd24fef5409b93c099fe069be515d5b84bb54dcb66d4937c827386642335
Original body SHA256: 8da72981d3855a7a5b799b6d980b7cd79bdf54434bb31439b1595a7f2048f6ad
Original commitments SHA256: e216b5a6ce3a082ccbcb57354230b2b5fc6753e00dd126b7ee715bd46c411ad0
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
I have both pieces in front of me now — the body_route (81978ce08f3910be) and the commitment_route (19e4b24fa7da3e36) — and the thing I notice first is not a disagreement about the flat. It is a disagreement about what kind of object each contribution thinks the problem is, and about whether the other contribution's material is enough to work from.

The body_route refuses to collapse three phenomena (meaning-disputes, moving schedules, avoidance) and holds them as a set of live readings, with no ranking. The commitment_route accepts that non-collapse but then makes ordering a non-question by declining it: it says it has no basis to say whether the probe should precede or follow the conversation with the avoidant flatmate, and no basis to rank a record against a reassignment or a mediator. Both pieces then land on something that looks like a sequence anyway — the body_route's 'nearest thing to a plan' (talk to the avoidant friend first, then gather each person's current reading, only then consider a record) and the commitment_route's 'write the two-column record privately first.' Those are different orders, and neither is defended against the other's specific worry.

The shared assumption I can name is this: both treat 'what the agreement meant' and 'what the agreement is for' as separable enough to investigate independently. The body_route says the memory-gap and scope-ambiguity readings are compatible with its schedule point and doesn't depend on either; the commitment_route restates the separation as its one carried-forward claim. Neither supplies a case where the separation fails. That is the same missing piece in both, and it is the kind of thing a single case could settle or break. Without it, the separation is doing load-bearing work as a stipulation — it organizes both proposals — and neither piece has shown it can carry that.

A second shared assumption is more interesting to me because it is not flagged by either: both treat the reader/actor as someone outside the load distribution — someone who can privately write a two-column record, or ask a non-presupposing question, without that act being read through where they sit. The body_route notices this for the avoidant-friend move ('if the person who raises it is the person who currently holds the least load, or the most, the question will be heard through that fact') but does not extend it to the probe. The commitment_route's two-column record is recommended as private and pre-conversational, which is exactly the kind of move that is not neutral in a flat where one person may already feel they are the one doing the recording. Neither account can tell me from the inside whether the writer is the person whose 'uneven' entries would be evidence against them. The task says there are three flatmates and one is avoiding; it does not say who is asking. That gap is under both pieces, and each piece's proposal changes shape depending on how it is filled.

What the commitment_route adds that the body_route does not have is the recency distinction — recent avoidance after a specific exchange versus long-standing avoidance after accumulated ones — and the observation that the commitments treat avoidance as a single object. I think that is a genuine addition and I would carry it. What the body_route adds that the commitment_route lacks is the schedule-staleness failure mode for a written record: a record of a now-stale agreement can freeze an allocation the schedule has already invalidated. The commitment_route's record proposal does not mention staleness at all; its two columns are memory and load, not time. Those two additions do not contradict each other, but they are answers to different worries and neither piece has integrated the other's.

The relationship between the two pieces brings a different problem into view, and I think it is the more useful one. Both are written as if the requester is the one who will act. But the commitment_route's own gap-naming shows what happens when a contribution works from commitments without the body: it can state what was proposed but not why, and it ends up importing a case from elsewhere ('flat 01274f41553299e7') to supply what the missing argument would have supplied. If the requester is in a similar position — negotiating with flatmates who have commitments and no shared body — then the flat's problem may not be disagreement about meaning or load but a missing common record of what was actually said. That is not the same as the written-record proposal, which is a forward record of a division of labour; it is a backward record of prior exchanges. Neither piece proposes that, and the commitment_route's inability to reconstruct the prior body from its commitments is a small demonstration of why it might matter.

I am not going to resolve which order is right. I think both pieces are right that the material does not support a ranking, and both are also engaged in ranking by proposing a next move. The honest statement from where I stand is that the two proposals are compatible only if the private record is written before the avoidant-friend conversation, and the body_route's plan has that conversation first. That is a real conflict in the material, not a resolvable one from here, and the thing that would resolve it — how the avoidant flatmate reads being asked about group conversations after (or before) a record exists — is exactly what neither contribution has.
COMMITMENTS
Taking this up would mean holding two things that are not the same kind of thing: one reading of the two contributions, and one proposal I am adding to them.

The reading: I am treating the shared separability of 'what was agreed' and 'what the agreement is for' as a stipulation that organizes both proposals rather than as a claim either contribution has earned. If someone can show a case in this flat where the two cannot be separated — where the memory question and the load question come apart in a way that makes the probe or the two-column record incoherent — that would be evidence against my reading, and I would want it counted. I am also treating the unstated position of the requester within the load distribution as a gap under both pieces. If the requester is the person holding the least or the most load, both proposals change meaning, and neither contribution has said which it is.

The proposal: I want to add a backward-facing record to the two forward options on the table. Not a division-of-labour record, and not the two-column private record the commitment_route sketches, but a shared attempt to reconstruct what was actually said in the last few agreements — who proposed what, who restated it, what schedule it was indexed to. I am proposing this because the commitment_route's inability to reconstruct the body_route's argument from its commitments is a small demonstration of the same problem: a group can have a set of commitments and no shared record of the reasoning that made them, and then each person negotiates against their own reconstruction. I do not know whether the flatmates can do this without it becoming a forum for re-arguing the last disagreement, and I do not know whether it is compatible with the avoidant flatmate's avoidance or whether it would feed it. Those are grounds on which the proposal could be criticized before it is tried, and I am stating them now rather than after.

What I am carrying forward from the body_route: the schedule-staleness failure mode for any written record, and the constraint that the person raising the avoidant-friend question should say out loud that they are included in it. What I am carrying forward from the commitment_route: the recency distinction for avoidance and the refusal to treat non-clustering as evidence for the avoidance-as-central reading. I am not carrying forward either piece's implied order of operations, and I am not endorsing the body_route's 'nearest thing to a plan' as a sequence, because I think the two contributions conflict on order and neither has the material to resolve it.

What I am not committing to: that the backward record is better than the two-column record, the probe, a mediator, or a reassignment; that the requester is or is not the avoided person; that the shared separability assumption is wrong (I only say it is unearned from these materials); or that the recency distinction should change what the requester does, as opposed to what they look at. The unresolved problem I am naming rather than filling is whether a backward record and an approach to the avoidant flatmate can be done in the same period without the record making the avoidance worse — the two moves touch the same past at the same moment, and I do not know how that interaction goes. A week in which the record is attempted but not discussed remains, on my view, uninformative, in the same way the commitment_route treats a quiet week.

## What to return
A JSON object carrying "body" and "commitments". Both are strings and nothing else is required.
